title: Norwegian star mittens
subtitle: Full mittens with an 8-pointed star border in two-colour stranded colourwork.
excerpt: Full mittens with an 8-pointed star border worked in two-colour stranded colourwork. DK weight, worked in the round, afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: 8-pointed star motifs appear in Norwegian mitten traditions documented by Annemor Sundbø in Setesdal Sweaters (2001) and in the Norwegian Folk Art collection at the National Museum Oslo. The specific chart here is derived from the common 8-round star found across multiple public-domain Norwegian pattern books from the 1900s.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stranded colourwork on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A knitting technique in which two or more yarns are carried across the back of the fabric. Only one colour is knitted at any point; the other floats across the inside. The floats should be no longer than 5 stitches to avoid snagging.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: , worked in DK weight wool in the round, with an 8-pointed star border at the cuff. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
The star band repeats over 8 rounds and 8 stitches. The main hand uses one colour; the cuff band and thumb use both. The construction is seamless, worked in the round using

content.text: 22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stranded colourwork on 3.75 mm needles. Stranded colourwork pulls tighter than stocking stitch. Use needles one size larger than your usual DK needles. Swatch the star chart specifically.

attrs.heading: 8-pointed star repeat (8 rounds x 8 sts, all rounds are RS, read right to left)

items.qty: k2 MC, k1 CC, k3 MC, k1 CC, k1 MC

content.text: The chart above reads as a simplified grid. Use the centre CC stitch on round 5 as your positioning check.
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 8 rounds of 2x2 rib in MC.
Join CC. Work the 8-round star chart. The stitch count (40, 44, 48) divides evenly into the 8-stitch repeat. Work 2 rounds in MC stocking stitch after the chart. Drop CC.
Continue in MC stocking stitch. At round 12 (14, 14) from the star band: work the first 10 (11, 12) stitches with waste yarn, slip back, work in MC to end. Continue for 18 (20, 22) more rounds.
Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before centre marker, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Graft or draw through.
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and 10 (11, 12) stitches below. Work 2 rounds of the star chart, then continue in MC. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds total. Bind off.
Floats visible from the outside: the float yarn is being caught too tightly. Keep an even tension on the floating yarn by spreading the stitches along the needle before drawing the float across.
Star looks lopsided: the chart start position shifted between repeat rounds. Check the beginning-of-round marker on every chart row.
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block the mittens by soaking in cool water and pinning flat to dry.
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Block after each wash to restore the colourwork.

The Selbu tradition uses the same 8-pointed star at a finer gauge across a full-body pattern covering cuff, hand, and thumb. The Selbu-style mittens pattern extends this construction into a more complex two-colour piece.
